english.title: Responsible person fail to prevent the causing of unnecessary suffering to an animal
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the person responsible for an animal, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ANIMAL..),

(A)_[an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), committed by **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[a failure to act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FAILURE..), by **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_

caused that animal to suffer, you permitted that to happen or failed to take such steps as were reasonable in all the circumstances to prevent that happening, and that suffering was unnecessary

english.notes:
(i) Section 2 of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides that a "Protected animal" is one of a kind which is commonly domesticated in the British Islands, is under the control of man whether on a permanent or temporary basis, or it is not living in a wild state.
(ii) The "failure to take steps" may be way of lack of supervision of the other person or otherwise.
(iii) Section 4(3) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides various relevant considerations with regard to determining whether suffering is unnecessary.
(iv) See section 33 for privation orders.
(v) See section 34 disqualification from owning keeping animals.
(vi) See section 35 for power to seize animals in connection with disqualification.
(vii) See section 37 for destruction in the interests of the animal.
(viii) See section 40 for the forfeiture of equipment used.
(ix) The maximum penalty for this offence has increased from 29th June 2021; for offences before that date see H8881/AW06002.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Note
Section 32(4A) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides that in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 2 to the Sentencing Act 2020, the reference to 12 months is to be read as a reference to 6 months.
